sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Diemen, next to Amsterdam, has regulated almost all of its parking and is wary of becoming Amsterdam's overflow. On 26 May 2025 the council adopted the Parkeerverordening Diemen 2025, in force from 1 July 2025, which provides for resident, business, visitor, car-share and carer permits [0]. Street parking costs 1.90 euros an hour in the centre around the Diemerplein, 1.20 euros an hour in the Bergwijkpark office area with a day card of 9.60 euros, and 0.10 euro an hour for the first 120 minutes along Muiderstraatweg and 1.90 euros after that, with a 25-euro day card in the permit zone [1][3]. The rules apply Monday to Saturday from 9:00 to 21:00, with some areas until 19:00, and not on Sundays [3]. The area in and around the centre is a blue zone with a two-hour limit, and the fine is 82 euros plus the parking fee [4]. Permits are valid only in the holder's own neighbourhood and cost 96 euros for two years for residents, and residents of Holland Park, Sniepkwartier and Punt Sniep cannot get street permits [6]. The scan car has enforced regulated parking since 2020, and the municipality also uses it to measure occupancy [5]. The Mobiliteitsvisie 2040, published on 10 July 2025, measured car ownership at 0.81 vehicles per household against 1.15 nationally and found parking pressure above the 85 percent threshold only in Diemen Noord and north of Hartveldseweg, where up to about 92 percent was measured in evening and night hours; it attributes part of this to residents and visitors of Amsterdam's IJburg parking more cheaply in Diemen [18]. A blue zone has been decided around Zeezigt [19].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The vision states ambitions and not decisions: reduce parking spaces where pressure is below 80 percent, in favour of greenery and bicycle parking, build an area-covering charging network, and introduce paid parking at the Diemen Zuid park-and-ride and shrink it to limit its use as a regional transfer point; the executive decided in April 2025 not to introduce environmental zones [19][17]. The Ouddiemerlaan rail underpass opened on 25 January 2023, and the station-side park-and-ride moved to the south side of the line, with a new green P&R beside the renewed Van Gemertplantsoen [15]. On 14 November 2024 the council adopted spatial requirements for the Harmoniehof, about 100 social rental homes on the former park-and-ride site on the Spoorzicht side, and the project page lists it as in the design phase, though it looks out of date [16]. A policy of 2019 counted 22 public charge posts and aimed to double them by 2020; later figures were not found [8]. A vehicle may use a charge-point bay only while charging, on pain of a 120-euro fine [7].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Paid parking began in June 2012 in the garage under the Diemerplein shopping centre, which the municipality does not run, in April 2018 in the Bergwijkpark office area and in October 2019 around Muiderstraatweg [10]. The Parkeerbeleidsplan 2021 recorded 7,505 regulated spaces, 1,100 paid or permit spaces and 6,405 in blue zones, with 5,500 resident permits, and says the car parks at the NS stations Diemen and Diemen Zuid were unregulated and filled from early morning, largely with commuters [9][12]. Since then, the Station Diemen car park has been operated solely by NS under a cooperation agreement of 2017, with a barrier and no maximum stay, according to council answers of March 2024, and train travellers get a discount [13]. NS announced a tariff sheet for 1 December 2026 listing the lot at 2.00 euros an hour, 8.50 euros a day and 2.50 euros a day for train travellers, under the name of the street beside it; those prices were not yet in force when we read them [14].

Our data cover the P+R Station Diemen, with 110 spaces, for about 59 days since 22 August 2026. Occupancy averaged about 26% on both weekdays and weekends, with a peak of 88% on a Saturday afternoon. The garage under the Diemerplein and the street parking are not in our data.
